Text to 3D.d: Generates a model from a text description.
Text to 3D.r: Describe a single object: what it is, shape, material, style. No background or scene.

Image to 3D.d: Generates a model from one image.
Image to 3D.r: Works best with one object, front view, fully in frame, plain background.

Image/Text to 3D.d: The main generator: a model from an image or from text.
Image/Text to 3D.r: If you have an image, use it — results are more accurate than from text.

Sketch to 3D.d: A model from a hand-drawn sketch plus a text description.
Sketch to 3D.r: Draw a clean outline of one object; describe material and style in the text.

Multi-View.d: Several photos of the same object from different sides (front, side, back).
Multi-View.r: Gives the most accurate shape, especially the back. Views should match in scale and lighting.

Multi-View to 3D.d: A model from several views of the same object.
Multi-View to 3D.r: At least 2 standard views: front + side or back.

Model to 3D.r: Useful to improve a rough or scanned model.

Geometry.r: Faster and cheaper. You can add a texture later.

Geometry + Texture.d: Shape with a color texture in one go.
Geometry + Texture.r: Choose it when you need a finished result in one step.

Untextured Model.d: A model without texture — geometry only.

Face Count.d: Number of polygons (faces). More means more detail, but a heavier model.
Face Count.r: Mobile/games: 5–30k. PC games: 30–100k. Rendering/printing: more is fine.

Set Face Count.d: Set an exact polygon count manually.

Auto Face Count.d: Polygon count is chosen automatically based on object complexity.

Smart Topology.d: Retopology: turns a heavy, messy mesh into a clean, light (low-poly) mesh with proper edge flow.
Smart Topology.r: Needed for games, animation and rigging. Can be skipped for static renders.

3D Smart Topology.d: Retopology: heavy mesh → clean, light low-poly model.
3D Smart Topology.r: Needed for games, animation and rigging.

Topology.d: The structure of the mesh — how polygons are laid out.

Retopology.d: Rebuilds the mesh into a clean and light one.
Retopology.r: Do it before rigging and animation.

Low-Poly.d: A model with few polygons — for games and real-time.

Low-poly.d: A model with few polygons — for games and real-time.

High-Poly Model.d: A detailed, heavy model (hundreds of thousands of polygons).
High-Poly Model.r: For rendering and printing. For games, retopologize first.

Quads.d: A mesh made of four-sided polygons.
Quads.r: Choose it if you will edit or animate the model in Blender/Maya — easier to work with.

Triangles.r: Choose it for direct import into a game engine (Unity/Unreal).

Low-Poly with Baked Normals.d: A light model plus a normal map that bakes fine detail from the high-poly model.
Low-Poly with Baked Normals.r: Best option for games: looks detailed with a low polygon count.

Low-Poly Without Normal Map.d: A light model without a normal map — detail is in the geometry only.
Low-Poly Without Normal Map.r: For stylized art, or if you will bake normals yourself.

Bake.d: Baking: transfers detail (normals, color) from a detailed model to the textures of a light one.

Bake Normals.d: Bake fine detail from the high-poly model into a normal map.
Bake Normals.r: Needed for game models after retopology.

UV Unwrap.d: UV unwrapping — "unfolds" the model onto a flat plane so a texture can be applied.
UV Unwrap.r: Needed if you will texture it yourself (Substance, Blender).

UV Unwrapping.d: UV unwrapping — "unfolds" the model onto a flat plane for texturing.
UV Unwrapping.r: Needed if you will texture it yourself.

Semantic UV.d: Smart unwrapping: seams follow meaningful parts (arm, head, chair leg).

Semantic UV Unwrap.d: Smart unwrapping: seams follow meaningful parts of the model.

Show UV Seams.d: Show UV seam lines on the model.

Texture.d: The color and material of the model's surface.

Texture Generation.d: Generates a texture for an existing model (yours or a generated one).
Texture Generation.r: Guide it with text or a reference image.

3D Texture Generation.d: Generates a texture for an existing model.
3D Texture Generation.r: Guide it with text or a reference image.

Text to Texture.d: A texture from a text description.
Text to Texture.r: Describe the material: "rusty metal", "polished wood", "anime style".

Image to Texture.d: A texture from a reference image.
Image to Texture.r: Best when the image matches the model's view (front view).

Multi-View to Texture.d: A texture from several views of the object.
Multi-View to Texture.r: Covers the sides and back most accurately.

Generate PBR Textures.d: PBR is a set of maps for realistic materials: color, metallic, roughness, normals.
Generate PBR Textures.r: Turn it on for games and realistic rendering.

Albedo.d: Base surface color without lighting or shadows.

Metallic.d: Metallic map: which parts of the surface are metal.

Roughness.d: Roughness map: matte (light) or glossy (dark) surface.

Normal.d: Normal map: fine surface relief without extra polygons.

Remove Baked Lighting.d: Removes painted-in lights and shadows from the texture, leaving clean color.
Remove Baked Lighting.r: Turn it on for games/PBR — lighting should come from the engine, not the texture.

Seamless Texture.d: A seamless (tileable) texture that can repeat like tiles.

Rigging & Skinning.d: Rigging adds a skeleton inside the model; skinning binds the mesh to the bones. Required for animation.
Rigging & Skinning.r: Works for humanoid characters. Model in T/A pose, facing forward.

Automatic Rigging.d: Places bones and binds the mesh automatically.
Automatic Rigging.r: Start with this; if bones are off, fix them manually.

Manual Rigging.d: Place key skeleton points (knees, elbows, etc.) by hand.
Manual Rigging.r: Use it if automatic rigging got it wrong.

Rigging & Animation.r: Needs a humanoid model in T/A pose.

Animation Generation.r: Pick a motion template or describe it with text/video.

3D Animation Generation.r: Pick a motion template or describe it with text/video.

Text to Motion.d: Motion from a text description ("walks and waves").

Video to Motion.d: Transfers motion from a video of a person to the model (video mocap).
Video to Motion.r: Fixed camera, whole body in frame, fitted clothing.

Motion Templates.d: Ready-made motions: walking, running, dancing, etc.

Component Split.d: Splits the model into separate parts — wheels, arms, drawers.
Component Split.r: Handy for editing, recoloring parts and animating mechanisms.

Component Segmentation.d: Splits the model into separate parts.

Pre-Split.d: Automatic preliminary split into parts before manual editing.
Pre-Split.r: Click it several times — results differ.

Part Mode.d: Part editing mode: clicking a face selects the whole part.

Seed.d: A number that controls randomness. Same seed + same settings = similar result.
Seed.r: Change it to get a different variant with the same settings.

Geometry Style.d: Shape style: realistic, cartoon, low-poly, etc.

Utilize symmetry.r: On for characters, vehicles, furniture. Off for asymmetric objects.

Model Version.d: Version of the neural network used for generation.
Model Version.r: Usually the newest is best; older ones if you liked their style.

Credits.d: In-app currency charged for each generation.

Native Editing.d: Edit a finished model with text commands.

Text to Scene.d: A 3D scene/world from a text description.

Select a Format.r: GLB — universal (Blender, web). FBX — Unity/Unreal and animation. OBJ — plain geometry. STL — 3D printing. USDZ — iPhone/AR.
